trigger: operator performs the documented ADR-0009 rollback procedure (starts the previous-release, pre-Postgres binary) after uninstalling a pack, while the retained legacy product-packs.db file was never mutated
policy_floor: ADR-0009 Decision section (normative MUST): 'a store with a wired erasure path must... delete the same subject/device from the rollback copy so rollback cannot resurrect data whose erasure was reported successful.' CORRECTION (this row supersedes pass-5's F035 row): the pass-5 'now SATISFIED' claim was an OVERCLAIM, independently caught by 4 of 6 Gate 8 reviewers (docs-writer, architect, cpp-expert, sre) reviewing commit 017d956e9. The fix (deleted_pack_ids tombstone table) closes the FORWARD-PATH hazard only (a redeployed/newly-joined replica's stale legacy file resurrecting a pack into shared Postgres) -- verified fixed, see F038/F039 below and the concurrency-race fix. It does NOT close the LITERAL clause: an operator rolling the server binary back to the pre-migration release reads product-packs.db directly, has no knowledge Postgres or deleted_pack_ids exist, and would see an uninstalled pack reappear for the duration of the rollback window. Two resolution paths identified (architect): (a) also mutate the legacy file at uninstall() time (partial benefit even then -- only protects the ONE replica that ran uninstall(), not the whole fleet's separate legacy-file copies, and conflicts with this store's own 'never mutates the legacy file' design invariant), or (b) an ADR-0009 update note (matching the existing ResponseStore/#2691 precedent in the same ADR) recording the tombstone substitution and explicitly accepting the residual rollback-window exposure as a recorded, deliberate risk. summary: FIXED: kProductPackDbErrorPrefix classification meant this deterministic, non-transient condition was reported as a RETRYABLE 503 -- compounding the F031/F033-tracked orphan risk (install_fn already ran against every sibling store with no lease held; a retry re-runs it again on every attempt, since the failure condition never clears). Added a duplicate-item_id pre-check before any Postgres interaction, returning a plain (non-db_error, 400-class) validation message instead. Outcome unchanged (whole install still fails) -- only the retryability classification changed.
rationale: New TEST_CASE 'ProductPackStore::install: a duplicate item id in one bundle fails as a plain validation error, never a retryable db_error' -- asserts the error message names the duplicate, does NOT carry kProductPackDbErrorPrefix, and confirms nothing was persisted to Postgres. Full ProductPackStore suite: 21 test cases (was 20), 483 assertions (was 477), all green.
